html:
Government by the adult male citizens of Athens, begun by the reforms of Cleisthenes in 508 BCE. Women, slaves and resident foreigners had no vote.

  • The Assembly of all citizens decided war, peace and laws, by show of hands.
  • The Council of 500, chosen by lot each year, prepared its business.
  • Juries of hundreds of citizens, also chosen by lot, judged cases. One of them condemned Socrates.
  • Generals were the main officials still elected, which is how Pericles led for so long.

Paying citizens for jury and council service let poor men take part. Macedon ended the system in 322 BCE.
sum: Government by the adult male citizens of Athens, begun by the reforms of Cleisthenes in 508 BCE. Women, slaves and resident foreigners had no vote.
